issue.title: Hand-edited research sidecar README (Topic Tags) makes init repo --check and every just check fail

task_type_fields.impact:
Every agent's `just check` / `sase tool run check` fails at `SASE validation` with
an UNKNOWN triage verdict, which invalidates prepared host-completion monitors
and forces recovery turns (seen on run 3891654a59c214244e5ab44bec12bdb1, ws12, and
734ca9c967854080278f0798d09b0048).
task_type_fields.repro:
In any sase workspace whose research sidecar is at or after research commit
`dcbfd0dc` ("docs(research): tag recent PyPI release reliability research",
2026-10-18 15:18Z, agent bbugyi200.apollo.8y), run:

```bash
.venv/bin/sase init repo --check --diff
```

It reports `~ update sase/repos/research/README.md −5` and wants to delete the
hand-added `## Topic Tags` section (the paragraph linking `TAGS.md`). Because
`sase validate` runs `init repo --check`, the `SASE validation` stage of
`just check` exits 1 in every workspace.

Root cause: the research sidecar README is an exact-match generated file
(`expected_sdd_sidecar_files` in `src/sase/sdd/_init_files.py` renders
`src/sase/sdd/templates/sidecar-research-README.md`), and dcbfd0dc edited it by
hand instead of changing the template. The template is shared by every project's
research sidecar, while `TAGS.md` exists only in sase's, so copying the section
into the template as-is would leave a broken link elsewhere.

Fix options: move the TAGS.md pointer out of the generated README and restore it
with `sase init repo`, or make tags a supported research-sidecar convention
(template section plus a generated or optional TAGS.md).

issue.creation_reason: Found while verifying an unrelated publish.yml change: the SASE validation stage fails in every workspace because the generated research README was edited by hand.
